doc.title: Lou Pallo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2007

title: Road work with the Hi Lads, Vegas and Spain
summary: Extended tours, life on the road, and short trips with Les Paul including a week in Spain; overseas audiences.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Right. Did you ever do any extended road work?
Oh yes. I’d be out like maybe two months, that was like Vegas, Reno, Tahoe, on different tours, it was with a group called the Hi Lads and we would tour all over.

It’s fun playing in different venues and especially playing Vegas and all that because all you have to do is bring your guitar with you. You pick your amp out. They have a room full of amps you say, “I’d like that amp at four o’clock in the afternoon” whatever time you go on. They’d have it out there set up with the wire. You just plug in and you’re all set. The controls would be all set for you. But living on the road after a while gets kind of rough. You have so many different clothes with you and so forth and you have to keep getting them cleaned because you can’t bring too much with you. And it’s lonesome in a way.
There’s a lot of down time, right?
Lot of down time and traveling time, especially when you’re driving from town to town. It’s fun. It’s an experience though.
Yeah. It’s something you should do but — © Fillius Jazz Archive -19-
I think it’s something you should do, try it, and then like now if we go on the road we fly out on a Tuesday, we perform on Wednesday, we’re back on Thursday, which is great. We’ll do one night.
Oh, oh well mostly with Les.

And the longest I’ve been away with Les was when we did Spain, that was a week. We flew out, we did a whole week in Spain and then flew back after that. That was The Expo — all the guitarists from all over the world. That was a great show.
A great show. But that’s the most in the past twenty years I guess, that I was away.
No. You mean as far as performing?
The reception you get overseas is fabulous, I mean the Europeans I guess, that’s where we were, they just appreciate everything you do.
